Procedural programming organizes a program as a sequence of instructions grouped into procedures or functions. C and Pascal are commonly taught in this style. C++, Java, Python, and BASIC can also be used procedurally, while supporting other programming styles too:
  • C
  • Pascal
  • Fortran
  • BASIC

Functional programming builds computations by composing function applications. It often favors immutable data and limits side effects, though languages differ in how strongly they enforce these ideas. Haskell, Erlang, Elixir, F#, and Scala support functional programming:
  • Haskell
  • Erlang
  • Elixir
  • F#
  • Scala

Object-oriented programming organizes software around objects that combine state with behavior. Classes are common, but languages can use other object models. This style can help structure programs; it does not automatically guarantee reuse or scalability. Java, Python, PHP, C++, and Ruby support object-oriented programming:
  • Java
  • Python
  • PHP
  • C++
  • Ruby

Scripting describes a common way of using languages for automation, system tasks, or interactive web behavior; it is not a separate programming paradigm. A script can use procedural, functional, or object-oriented ideas. Examples commonly used for scripting include:
  • JavaScript
  • PHP
  • Ruby
  • Python
  • Bash
  • Perl

Logic programming represents relationships with facts and rules, then uses queries to derive answers. The language runtime searches for solutions that satisfy the rules. Prolog and Datalog are examples; logic programming is also a declarative style:
  • Prolog
  • Datalog
